cues.text: This equation measures a resistance in the lungs.
Start with the mean pulmonary artery pressure,
and subtract the mean pulmonary capillary wedge pressure.
then divide by the cardiac output.
The result is the pulmonary vascular resistance.
So: the pressure difference across the lungs, times 80, divided by cardiac output.
Its reference range is 125 to 250 dynes × sec/cm³.
